19	import java.util.Locale;
20	
21	import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
22	
23	/**
24	 * Builds an owner's {@code customerCode}, formatted {@code '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>'} where CITY3 is
25	 * the upper-cased first three letters of the city, LAST3 the upper-cased first three letters of the
26	 * last name, and NNNN a per-city 4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one more than the number of
27	 * owners already in that city (e.g. {@code 'LON-SMI-0007'}).
28	 */
29	@Component
30	public class CustomerCodeGenerator {
31	
32	    /**
33	     * @param city          the owner's city, used for the CITY3 prefix
34	     * @param lastName      the owner's last name, used for the LAST3 prefix
35	     * @param cityOwnerCount the number of owners already stored in that city; the sequence is one greater
36	     * @return the formatted customer code
37	     */
38	    public String generate(String city, String lastName, long cityOwnerCount) {
39	        return String.format("%s-%s-%04d", abbreviate(city), abbreviate(lastName), cityOwnerCount + 1);
40	    }
41	
42	    private String abbreviate(String value) {
43	        return value.substring(0, Math.min(3, value.length())).toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);
44	    }
45	}

36	     * Look up the entity of the given class with the given id in the given collection.
37	     *
38	     * @param entities    the collection to search
39	     * @param entityClass the entity class to look up
40	     * @param entityId    the entity id to look up
41	     * @return the found entity
42	     * @throws ObjectRetrievalFailureException if the entity was not found
43	     */
44	    public static <T extends BaseEntity> T getById(Collection<T> entities, Class<T> entityClass, int entityId)
45	        throws ObjectRetrievalFailureException {
46	        for (T entity : entities) {

My design:
- A single pure `BusinessDay` helper (weekend→next weekday roll), reused everywhere.
- `Owner` `@PrePersist` enforces the invariant on the *stored* date (default-to-today, then roll) — this covers both supplied and defaulted dates, and the derived `membershipNumber` automatically follows.
- `DailyOwnerLimitValidator` counts against that same effective business day.

## Summary

I implemented the business-day rule for the effective registration date. The change funnels the weekend→Monday roll through one reusable helper and applies it consistently to the stored date, all derived values, and the daily create-limit.

**New file — `model/BusinessDay.java`**: a small, single-purpose helper with `onOrAfter(LocalDate)` — returns a weekday unchanged, rolls Saturday forward 2 days and Sunday forward 1 day to the next Monday.

**`model/Owner.java`** — the `@PrePersist` callback (renamed `resolveRegistrationDate`) now defaults the date to today when absent *and then* rolls the effective date off weekends. Because `getMembershipNumber()` derives its `M<YY>` year segment from the stored `registrationDate` field, the membership number automatically uses the adjusted date. This covers both cases — a supplied weekend date is now rolled forward too, not just the defaulted one.

**`rest/validation/DailyOwnerLimitValidator.java`** — `validate()` now takes the client-supplied registration date (nullable), computes the same effective business day via `BusinessDay.onOrAfter(supplied ?? today)`, and counts owners registered on that adjusted day (and reports it in the exception).

**`rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — passes `ownerFieldsDto.getRegistrationDate()` into the validator so the limit check keys off the request's supplied date.

The substantive logic (the weekend roll) lives in exactly one place and is reused by the entity and the validator; each caller keeps only its own trivial "supplied-or-today" defaulting in the layer where that context lives. No class took on unrelated responsibilities.
